ranked.headline: Single-cell models separate technical noise from cell state, kinetics and spatial context
ranked.summary: New methods explicitly model noise, transcriptional bursting, raw-molecule spatial structure and cohort-level disease programs in single-cell data.

ranked.headline: Energy, dynamics and geometry supervision is being folded into sequence foundation models
ranked.summary: Variant-effect and ligand-scoring predictors now train on MD, force-field energy and residue-atom geometry rather than sequence statistics alone, feeding closed-loop design.

ranked.headline: Perturbation response models face stricter delta metrics and confounder disentanglement
ranked.summary: New perturbation models arrive as benchmarks show global Pearson inflates performance and drug-induced responses concord poorly across datasets.

ranked.headline: Scalable tools and catalogues for pathogen genomes, mobile elements and viral variation
ranked.summary: Offline nanopore diagnostics, alignment-free viral variant calling and planetary-scale MGE and prophage resources broaden practical microbial genome analysis.

ranked.headline: Spatial domains and single-cell partitions gain formal significance tests
ranked.summary: SigDoTS and ProClust add null-model testing to domain and cell-group calls, while benchmarks probe sequencing-depth and network-estimation limits.

ranked.headline: Histology guides inference of continuous, large-panel and higher-resolution spatial gene expression
ranked.summary: New preprints use histology to extend sparse spatial transcriptomics into 3D and large gene panels, while others refine resolution and spatial statistics.

ranked.headline: Pretrained protein models are applied to site and variant prediction and then tested for failure modes
ranked.summary: New preprints pair protein language model applications with stress tests: relabeling invariance, embedding anisotropy and NMR shift errors expose limits of learned representations.

ranked.headline: Single-cell and spatial perturbation screens resolve stage-dependent regulatory wiring in differentiation
ranked.summary: Three preprints pair CRISPR perturbation or enhancer-network analysis with differentiation models to resolve dynamic, condition-specific regulatory architecture.

ranked.headline: Generative and language-model design extends binders to multi-variant, multi-epitope and motif-level targets
ranked.summary: Preprints this week pair experimental readouts with design across antigen variants, IgE removal, de novo proteins and PDZ peptides, alongside a CDR language-model paper.

ranked.headline: Structure-linked annotation databases expand content and add machine-actionable access
ranked.summary: Six database updates pair added structural and annotation content with versioned APIs, MCP servers or workflows, enabling programmatic and agentic querying.

ranked.headline: Static structure prediction is being extended to conformational ensembles and dynamics
ranked.summary: Seven preprints from 9-16 November pair AI structure predictors and generative models with enhanced sampling and MD to resolve ensembles, not single folds.

ranked.headline: Models link biophysical constraints to emergent circuit dynamics from dendrites to visual cortex
ranked.summary: Four new studies tie dendritic, spiking and connectome constraints to network dynamics, showing that matched tuning or outputs can hide distinct underlying regimes.

ranked.headline: Cancer models infer missing modalities and clone identity by linking molecular, imaging and clinical data
ranked.summary: Seven preprints link scRNA-seq, copy-number, histopathology and mutation data to assign clones, predict missing modalities and refine survival prognosis.

ranked.headline: Connectome-constrained inferences are audited against unmeasured physiology and operation-induced functional error
ranked.summary: Two preprints stress-test connectome structure-function claims, auditing operations on C. elegans and tuning physiology fairly across Drosophila wirings.

ranked.headline: Open pipelines and evaluation criteria for structure-based ligand and complex modeling
ranked.summary: Predicted structures now feed screening and design, so ensembles, pose metrics, membrane checks and confidence filters need scrutiny.

ranked.headline: Computational models link actomyosin filament mechanics and turnover to force transmission and tissue form
ranked.summary: Four November 2026 preprints apply mechanistic actomyosin models from cortex and perinuclear actin to cell contacts and wing disc morphogenesis.

ranked.headline: Multi-omics atlases and databases are paired with embedded analysis tools for disease interpretation
ranked.summary: Atlas, database and modeling reports this period tie omics data to disease context, from a 12.6M-cell atlas to kinase mutation–drug response.

ranked.headline: Genomic language model embeddings are benchmarked and adapted for viral and bacterial taxonomy and surveillance
ranked.summary: New preprints benchmark genomic language model embeddings against k-mer and MinHash baselines and adapt ProkBERT for pathogen surveillance.

ranked.headline: Sequence-aware and multimodal models of somatic mutation, plus a canine tumor driver resource
ranked.summary: Three items extend cancer mutation modeling: joint SBS/DBS/ID inference, sequence-based substitution prediction, and a harmonized canine exome atlas.

ranked.headline: Peptide ADMET databases and multimodal predictors emerge alongside audit-ready evaluation standards
ranked.summary: New peptide ADMET resources and models arrive as evaluation work questions leakage and exposure-blind ranking in drug prediction.

ranked.headline: Curated multi-species resources extend noncoding RNA annotation and translation evidence
ranked.summary: Expanding cross-species RNA databases and a non-model bat genome assembly add genomic context and translation evidence for noncoding RNAs.

ranked.headline: Built-in assumption checks and randomization steps in computational biology pipelines
ranked.summary: Recent preprints embed validity checks such as assumption screening and identifiability classification directly into analysis workflows.

ranked.headline: Computational inference of RNA from sequence, raw current, and mass spectra
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and publications apply deep learning and spectral methods to RNA therapeutic design and direct molecular measurement.

ranked.headline: Curated microbial metabolic resources link enzyme diversity to bacterial function
ranked.summary: Expanded metabolic models, pathway annotation, and enzyme prediction tools are updating how microbial genome-scale function is inferred from sequence.

ranked.headline: Isoform-resolved atlases link transcript variation to traits and regulatory loci
ranked.summary: Long-read and multi-tissue RNA-seq resources now map isoform-level regulation to complex traits across lettuce, sheep, and mouse.

ranked.headline: Single-cell multiomics map regulatory programs across basal ganglia and adult brain
ranked.summary: Joint chromatin and transcriptome profiling at single-cell resolution now spans human, mouse and primate basal ganglia, with population-level variation.

ranked.headline: Tools link cis-regulatory elements to target genes via multiomics and chromatin contacts
ranked.summary: Recent releases extend plant regulatory resources to 240 species and add Hi-C-based target gene inference alongside interactive plant RNA-seq exploration.

ranked.headline: Quantitative tests of computational models against neural and behavioral data
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and a published method pair biologically realistic inputs and memory structure with quantitative fits to neural and behavioral data.

ranked.headline: Inferring interaction-driven cell dynamics from single-cell and spatial transcriptomics
ranked.summary: Time-resolved and snapshot spatial data now allow learning explicit cell-cell interaction terms within inferred cell dynamics, including nonreciprocal couplings.

ranked.headline: Graphs pair topology with auxiliary knowledge for gene and protein network inference
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and a published method pair graph topology with sequence, ontology, or pairwise features for single-cell and protein network inference.

ranked.headline: Hybrid mechanistic and learned models advance quantitative forecasting of pathogen spread
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and publications extend forecasting with memory terms, simulation-informed training, and sequence-derived features.

ranked.headline: Gene content inventories built from multi-genome evidence, not single references
ranked.summary: Progressive Cactus alignments, orthogroup mapping and PANTHER 2027 extend gene content delimitation beyond single-reference annotation.

ranked.headline: Pretrained generative biomolecular models repurposed beyond their original training objectives
ranked.summary: Reusing existing generative architectures and their outputs enables zero-shot and training-free design across protein complexes, molecules, RNA, and antibodies.

ranked.headline: Count-based and sequence models map regulatory variant effects across cell types
ranked.summary: Donor-level expression and chromatin data now support genetic effect models that capture cell-type structure and noncoding variant impact.

ranked.headline: Integrated omics resources link methylation, GWAS, expression and spatial data to context
ranked.summary: Five 2026 database releases extend cancer methylation, GWAS, transcriptomic and spatial resources with analysis modules for expert reuse.

ranked.headline: Harmonized metadata and automated reprocessing make public sequence archives reusable
ranked.summary: Cross-study reuse of public sequence and omics data depends on harmonized metadata, standardized processing, and maintained archive interfaces.

ranked.headline: Polymer models link chromosome structure, loop extrusion and looping measurements
ranked.summary: Polymer simulations now infer chromosome dynamics from Hi-C and test how well microscopy and single-molecule readouts constrain chromatin looping.

ranked.headline: Learned models recover structure from noisy cryo-EM/ET and fluorescence microscopy data
ranked.summary: Learned models with data-derived constraints are being applied to cryo-EM/ET particle classification and cryo-ET tilt-series denoising.

ranked.headline: LLM agents are driving biological experiments, simulations and model construction
ranked.summary: Agentic LLM systems now drive robotic culture, molecular dynamics and systems-biology workflows, making auditability a design requirement.

ranked.headline: Compressed indexes speed k-mer queries and exact matching in large genome collections
ranked.summary: Terabase assembly collections push k-mer and exact-match queries toward compressed, sublinear-space indexes.
